questions.q: The annual festival bonus of a company is distributed entirely between two top managers, X and Y. Last year, X's bonus was ₹40,000 less than Y's bonus. This year, the total bonus pool remains exactly the same, but X's performance improved, increasing his share by 20%. As a result, X now receives ₹20,000 more than Y. What is the total bonus pool of the company?
questions.s: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM / Deviation: $A + B = K$ (Total bonus is constant. We will use the $\frac{D_2 - D_1}{2}$ Difference Hack). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Pura question dekh Pehle X peeche tha, ab X aage hai. Aur total sum fix hai! Seedha difference ka shift dekh aur 2 se divide maar, X ka exact increment bahar aa jayega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Let's apply the Ultimate Difference Hack: Purana Difference ($X - Y$) = -40,000 (Kyuki X kam tha Y se). Naya Difference ($X - Y$) = +20,000 (Kyuki X ab Y se aage hai). Is pure transaction mein X ka actual profit (Net Change) kitna hua? $\text{Increment in X} = \frac{\text{New Diff} - \text{Old Diff}}{2}$ $\text{Increment in X} = \frac{20000 - (-40000)}{2} = \frac{60000}{2} = 30,000. Toh bhai, X ka bonus ₹30,000 badha hai. Lekin question kehta hai ki X ka bonus 20% (yani $1/5$) badha hai. Seedha equate kar de: X ka $1/5 = 30,000$ $\Rightarrow \text{Purana X} = 30,000 \times 5 = 1,50,000. Ab Y nikal le: Purane case mein X, Y se ₹40,000 kam tha. Toh Y kitna hoga? $\text{Purana Y} = 1,50,000 + 40,000 = 1,90,000. Total Bonus = $\text{Purana X} + \text{Purana Y}$ $\Rightarrow 1,50,000 + 1,90,000 = 3,40,000. (Option 3 is correct. 10 seconds flat!) Method 2 (Concept Builder - Basics): Let Total Bonus = $K$. Initial Case: $X + Y = K$ aur $Y - X = 40000$. Solve karne par: $X = \frac{K - 40000}{2}$. New Case: X gets 20% more, so New X = $1.2X$. Since total is $K$, New Y = $K - 1.2X$. Given condition: New X - New Y = $20000$. $\Rightarrow 1.2X - (K - 1.2X) = 20000$ $\Rightarrow 2.4X - K = 20000$ Substitute $K = 2X + 40000$: $\Rightarrow 2.4X - (2X + 40000) = 20000$ $\Rightarrow 0.4X = 60000 \Rightarrow X = 150000$. $K = 2(150000) + 40000 = 340000$. Future Exam Takeaway: Elections ho, profit sharing ho, ya salary distribution—agar "Total Sum" fix hai aur do logon ka "Lead/Deficit" diya hai, toh seedha $\frac{D_2 - D_1}{2}$ lagao. Ye hack tujhe equation banane se bacha lega aur time bacha ke dega!

questions.q: A salesman has done total sale of Rs. (x + 17000) and the rate of commission up to Rs. (x + 5000) is $13.33\%$ and after Rs. (x + 5000), he gets some bonus amount which is equal to Rs. (x - 8000). If the bonus rate is $16.66\%$ on the amount exceeding Rs. (x + 5000), then find his total sale.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh TestRipper, 'x' dekh ke darna nahi hai. Dono range '(x+17000)' aur '(x+5000)' form me hain. Difference lega toh x gayab! Seedha excess amount nikal aayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Excess sale = $(x + 17000) - (x + 5000) = 12000$. Bonus mila is excess ka $16.66\%$ yani $1/6$. Bonus $= 2000$. Question me bonus $(x - 8000)$ hai. $x - 8000 = 2000 \implies x = 10000$. Total sale thi $x+17000$, seedha 27000 answer mark kar!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Excess} = (x + 17000) - (x + 5000) = 12000$
$\text{Bonus} = 12000 \times \frac{1}{6} = 2000$
$x - 8000 = 2000 \implies x = 10000$
$\text{Total} = 10000 + 17000 = 27000$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraically poori condition likh, rate of commission wagera add kar. Uski yahan zaroorat nahi thi kyunki excess bonus direct de rakha hai aur bonus ki condition bhi.

Mathematically :-
$\text{Total Sale} = S = x + 17000$
$\text{Bonus} = \frac{1}{6}(S - (x + 5000))$
$\text{Bonus} = \frac{12000}{6} = 2000$
$x - 8000 = 2000 \implies x = 10000$
$S = 27000$

Exam Takeaway: Variables dekh kar panic nahi karna, variables difference lete hi khud eliminate ho jate hain.

questions.q: If the height of a circular cone is increased by 33.33% and its radius is increased by 12.5%, then what will be the change in its volume?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Cone ki volume $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ hoti hai. Wo $\frac{1}{3}\pi$ jaise constants ratio nikalte waqt kat jaate hain. Farak sirf $r^2 \times h$ padta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, fraction multipliers bana.
$h$ badha $33.33\%$ yani $+\frac{1}{3} \implies \frac{4}{3}$.
$r$ badha $12.5\%$ yani $+\frac{1}{8} \implies \frac{9}{8}$.
Volume Multiplier $= (\frac{9}{8})^2 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{81}{64} \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{27}{16}$.
Matlab volume 16 se badh kar 27 ho gayi. Increment hua 11 ka.
Percentage chnage $= \frac{11}{16} \times 100 = 11 \times 6.25\% = 68.75\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Isme purana method $a+b+\frac{ab}{100}$ lagana muskil hai kyu ki 3 variables hain (r, r, h). Isiliye fractional chain ratio method sabse best hai.

Exam Takeaway: Standard base fractions ko tips pe rakh, jaise $\frac{1}{16} = 6.25\%$.

questions.q: Weight of Ayush and Abhishek are in the ratio of 8:5. Abhishek's weight increases by 40 percent and total weight of Ayush and Abhishek both increases by 60 percent. If total weight becomes 104 kg, then what is the weight of Ayush after the increment?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh TestRipper bhai, pure group ka weight 60% bada, par ek banda sirf 40% bada, yani usne apne hisse ka 20% ghapla kiya. Dusre bande ko compensation dena padega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total deviation = Abhishek ne 5 unit par $-20\%$ ka deficit diya yani $-100\%$. Ye kami Ayush poori karega apne 8 unit par. Toh Ayush badhega $= 60\% + (100/8)\% = 72.5\%$. Total weight naya 104 hai, purana $104/1.6 = 65$ tha. Purana Ayush $= (8/13) \times 65 = 40$. Naya Ayush = $40 \times 1.725 = 69$ kg. Solid concept!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Deficit} = 5 \times (40-60) = -100\%$
$\text{Ayush Inc} = 60 + \frac{100}{8} = 72.5\%$
$\text{Old Total} = \frac{104}{1.6} = 65$
$\text{Old Ayush} = 65 \times \frac{8}{13} = 40$
$\text{New Ayush} = 40 \times 1.725 = 69$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $8x$ aur $5x$ maan. Dono ko add karke equation set up kar, solve karne me pasina aayega.

Mathematically :-
$8x + 5x = 13x$
$13x \times 1.6 = 104 \implies 20.8x = 104 \implies x = 5$
$\text{Ayush}_{old} = 40, \text{Abhishek}_{old} = 25$
$\text{Abhishek}_{new} = 25 \times 1.4 = 35$
$\text{Ayush}_{new} = 104 - 35 = 69$

Exam Takeaway: JSM Deviation method se badhe se badhe weighted average ke questions tod sakte ho.

questions.q: In a school the number of students who reads math only is double to who reads only English and the number of students who reads both is one third to who did not read any. If 28 students read both subject and 400 students are in the school (i) Find number of student who read only English (ii) Find number of student who read Math.
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Both = 28. Neither = $28 \times 3 = 84$. Total bach gaye: $400 - (28+84) = 288$. Ye 288 bache sirf Only Math aur Only English ke. Ratio Only_Math : Only_Eng = 2:1. Yani 3 parts = 288, 1 part (Only English) = 96. Total Math padhne wale = Only Math (192) + Both (28) = 220. Option 1 straight matching!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Mental Venn Diagram.

Mathematically :-
$$ B = 28, \quad N = 3 \times 28 = 84 \\ M_o + E_o = 400 - (B + N) = 400 - 112 = 288 \\ M_o = 2E_o \implies 3E_o = 288 \implies E_o = 96 \\ M_{\text{Total}} = M_o + B = 192 + 28 = 220 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full Set Theory expansion.

Mathematically :-
$$ U = M \cup E + N \\ M \cup E = M_o + E_o + B \\ U = M_o + E_o + B + N \\ 400 = 2x + x + 28 + (3 \times 28) \\ 400 = 3x + 112 \implies 3x = 288 \implies x = 96 \\ \text{Only English} = x = 96 \\ \text{Math Total} = M_o + B = 2x + 28 = 192 + 28 = 220 $$

Exam Takeaway: Set theory without formulas, sirf parts ke form me visualise karo.

questions.q: A fruit seller sells 40% of the oranges that he has along with 4 more oranges to a customer. he then sells 25% of the remaining oranges and 4 more oranges to second customer. he then sells 80% of the now remaining oranges to a third customer and is still left with 4 oranges. How many oranges did the fruit seller have initially?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, ulta chal! C3 ke paas jaane ke baad 4 bache, ye $20\%$ hain kyunki usko $80\%$ de diye the. Toh C3 ke paas total remaining the 20. C2 ne 4 extra liye the, wapas do = 24. Ye 24 $75\%$ the, toh total the 32. C1 ne 4 extra liye, wapas do = 36. Ye 36 $60\%$ the, toh shuru me the 60. Pure reverse thinking!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Reverse working approach.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{End: } 20\% \text{ of } R_2 = 4 \implies R_2 = 20 \\ \text{Step 2: } 75\% \text{ of } R_1 - 4 = R_2 = 20 \\ 75\% \text{ of } R_1 = 24 \implies R_1 = \frac{24}{0.75} = 32 \\ \text{Step 1: } 60\% \text{ of Initial} - 4 = R_1 = 32 \\ 60\% \text{ of Initial} = 36 \implies \text{Initial} = \frac{36}{0.6} = 60 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Forward logic basic equation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Let total } = x \\ \text{After C1: } R_1 = x - (0.4x + 4) = 0.6x - 4 \\ \text{After C2: } R_2 = R_1 - (0.25 R_1 + 4) = 0.75 R_1 - 4 \\ \text{After C3: } R_3 = R_2 - 0.8 R_2 = 0.2 R_2 \\ 0.2 R_2 = 4 \implies R_2 = 20 \\ 0.75 R_1 - 4 = 20 \implies 0.75 R_1 = 24 \implies R_1 = 32 \\ 0.6x - 4 = 32 \implies 0.6x = 36 \implies x = 60 $$

Exam Takeaway: Remaining problems me jab constant values judd rahi ho toh 'Reverse Logic' sabse accurate aur fast hoti hai.

questions.q: P, Q, R and S have different amounts. Q has 2.5 times the amount 'p' has. 's' has 40% less than Q. The amount R has equals the average of all four persons. If the sum of amounts of P and R is 4800, find the amount of R has. (CHSL TIER I - 19/11/2025 - SHIFT 2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: 40% less ka matlab uske paas 60% hai. Toh $0.6 \times 2.5 = 1.5$. Sabko ek base variable $P$ me convert kar lenge toh equation single variable ki ban jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, sabko line me laga.
$Q = 2.5P$.
$S = 60\% \text{ of } Q = 0.6 \times 2.5P = 1.5P$.
R sabka average hai: $4R = P + Q + R + S \implies 3R = P + 2.5P + 1.5P = 5P \implies R = \frac{5}{3}P$.
Ab given hai $P + R = 4800 \implies P + \frac{5}{3}P = \frac{8}{3}P = 4800 \implies P = 1800$.
Toh $R = 4800 - 1800 = 3000$. Ekdum badiya set hua!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Isko ratios me tod le: $P:Q:S = 1:2.5:1.5 = 2:5:3$.
Inka sum = 10 units. $R = \frac{10+R}{4} \implies 3R = 10 \implies R = \frac{10}{3}$.
$P+R = 2 + \frac{10}{3} = \frac{16}{3} \equiv 4800$. $1 \text{ unit} = 900$. Toh $R = \frac{10}{3} \times 900 = 3000$.

Exam Takeaway: Decimals se ghabra mat, ek fixed base me equations ko scale kar le, zindagi asaan ho jayegi.

questions.q:
A retail store sells Premium and Casual shirts. The ratio of the price of a Premium shirt to a Casual shirt is 5:2. The ratio of the daily volume of units sold of Premium to Casual shirts is 2:15, generating a fixed combined daily revenue of $50,000.

Due to a market shift, the price of Casual shirts is increased by 20%, but their sales volume drops by 10%. To maintain the exact same total daily revenue of $50,000, by what percentage must the overall revenue generated by Premium shirts decrease?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change + Zero-Sum (JSM) Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan Revenue = Price $\times$ Volume hai. Casual shirts ke price aur volume dono me change hai, toh pehle inka single net successive nikal le. $+20$ aur $-10$ ka successive aayega $+8\%$. Ab total revenue ka ratio nikal (Premium : Casual = $10 : 30 = 1 : 3$). Casual (Base 3) ne total 8% ki vridhi ki, yani $+24$ ka deviation. Total fix rakhne ke liye Premium (Base 1) ko seedha $-24$ girna padega. Khel khatam! 50,000 bas darane ke liye hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle successive laga, fir JSM se balance kar de. Mathematically :-
$\text{Revenue Ratio (Prem : Cas)} = (5 \times 2) : (2 \times 15) = 10 : 30 = 1 : 3$
$\text{Casual Net Change} = 20 - 10 - \frac{20 \times 10}{100} = +8\%$
$\text{Casual Deviation} = 3 \times 8\% = +24$
$\text{Required Premium Loss} = -24$
$\% \text{ Reduction in Premium} = \frac{24}{1} = 24\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute numbers maan kar solve karna. Mathematically :-
$\text{Let Total Revenue} = 400x$
$\text{Initial Premium Rev} = 100x, \text{Casual Rev} = 300x$
$\text{New Casual Rev} = 300x \times 1.08 = 324x$
$\text{Required Premium Rev} = 400x - 324x = 76x$
$\text{Reduction in Premium} = 100x - 76x = 24x$
$\% \text{ Reduction} = \frac{24x}{100x} \times 100 = 24\%$ Exam Takeaway: Jab $A \times B$ ke dono components change hon, toh pehle Successive lagakar usko single percentage me compress kar lo. Fir Base Ratio par Zero-Sum lagao. Ye 2 steps me khatam hone wala topper method hai.

questions.q: The population of country A decreased by p% and the population of country B decreased by q% from the year 2020 to 2021. Here 'p' is greater than 'q'. Let 'x' be the ratio of the population of country A to the population of country B in the given year. What is the percentage decrease in 'x' from 2020 to 2021?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change / Variable Ratio Algebra

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Formula based hai. Ratio $x = \frac{A}{B}$. New ratio banega $x' = \frac{A(1 - \frac{p}{100})}{B(1 - \frac{q}{100})}$. Yaani old ke sath ek multiplier chipka hai $\frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Bas yahi se decrease fraction nikal lena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... New $x' = x \times \frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Decrease kitna hua? $(1 - \frac{100-p}{100-q}) \times x = \frac{(100-q) - (100-p)}{100-q} \times x = \frac{p-q}{100-q} \times x$. Percentage me badalne ke liye 100 se multiply karo base (x) ke respect me: $\frac{p-q}{100-q} \times 100$. Option A tick maar bina darr ke!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Value assume karlo. Let A=100, B=100. Let p=20, q=10. Original x=1. New A=80, New B=90. New x = $\frac{80}{90} = \frac{8}{9}$. Decrease = $1 - \frac{8}{9} = \frac{1}{9}$. Percentage decrease = $\frac{100}{9}\%$. Options me p=20, q=10 dalo. A) $\frac{100(10)}{90} = \frac{100}{9}$. Match! Baki options match nahi karenge.

Future Exam Takeaway: Variables dekh ke blank mat ho, assumption method (Method 2) hamesha zinda rakhega.

Due to a 20% salary hike, her income increases. However, her household expenses also rise by 10%, her entertainment costs increase by 12% while her expenses on education remain unchanged. Radha decides to save any leftover income after adjusting these changes. What is the percentage increase in Radha's savings?

Savings kitni badhi? $33.6 - 20 = 13.6$.
Percentage increment $= \frac{13.6}{20} \times 100 = 68\%$.

The difference of votes secured by the candidate standing 3rd to the candidate standing 4th is equal to 69198. Find the votes secured by the winning candidate.

questions_hin.q_hi: The annual festival bonus of a company is distributed entirely between two top managers, X and Y. Last year, X's bonus was ₹40,000 less than Y's bonus. This year, the total bonus pool remains exactly the same, but X's performance improved, increasing his share by 20%. As a result, X now receives ₹20,000 more than Y. What is the total bonus pool of the company?
questions_hin.s_hi: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 3. JSM / Deviation: $A + B = K$ (Total bonus is constant. We will use the $\frac{D_2 - D_1}{2}$ Difference Hack). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Pura question dekh Pehle X peeche tha, ab X aage hai. Aur total sum fix hai! Seedha difference ka shift dekh aur 2 se divide maar, X ka exact increment bahar aa jayega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Let's apply the Ultimate Difference Hack: Purana Difference ($X - Y$) = -40,000 (Kyuki X kam tha Y se). Naya Difference ($X - Y$) = +20,000 (Kyuki X ab Y se aage hai). Is pure transaction mein X ka actual profit (Net Change) kitna hua? $\text{Increment in X} = \frac{\text{New Diff} - \text{Old Diff}}{2}$ $\text{Increment in X} = \frac{20000 - (-40000)}{2} = \frac{60000}{2} = 30,000. Toh bhai, X ka bonus ₹30,000 badha hai. Lekin question kehta hai ki X ka bonus 20% (yani $1/5$) badha hai. Seedha equate kar de: X ka $1/5 = 30,000$ $\Rightarrow \text{Purana X} = 30,000 \times 5 = 1,50,000. Ab Y nikal le: Purane case mein X, Y se ₹40,000 kam tha. Toh Y kitna hoga? $\text{Purana Y} = 1,50,000 + 40,000 = 1,90,000. Total Bonus = $\text{Purana X} + \text{Purana Y}$ $\Rightarrow 1,50,000 + 1,90,000 = 3,40,000. (Option 3 is correct. 10 seconds flat!) Method 2 (Concept Builder - Basics): Let Total Bonus = $K$. Initial Case: $X + Y = K$ aur $Y - X = 40000$. Solve karne par: $X = \frac{K - 40000}{2}$. New Case: X gets 20% more, so New X = $1.2X$. Since total is $K$, New Y = $K - 1.2X$. Given condition: New X - New Y = $20000$. $\Rightarrow 1.2X - (K - 1.2X) = 20000$ $\Rightarrow 2.4X - K = 20000$ Substitute $K = 2X + 40000$: $\Rightarrow 2.4X - (2X + 40000) = 20000$ $\Rightarrow 0.4X = 60000 \Rightarrow X = 150000$. $K = 2(150000) + 40000 = 340000$. Future Exam Takeaway: Elections ho, profit sharing ho, ya salary distribution—agar "Total Sum" fix hai aur do logon ka "Lead/Deficit" diya hai, toh seedha $\frac{D_2 - D_1}{2}$ lagao. Ye hack tujhe equation banane se bacha lega aur time bacha ke dega!

Mental Venn Diagram.

$$ B = 28, \quad N = 3 \times 28 = 84 \\ M_o + E_o = 400 - (B + N) = 400 - 112 = 288 \\ M_o = 2E_o \implies 3E_o = 288 \implies E_o = 96 \\ M_{\text{Total}} = M_o + B = 192 + 28 = 220 $$

Full Set Theory expansion.

$$ U = M \cup E + N \\ M \cup E = M_o + E_o + B \\ U = M_o + E_o + B + N \\ 400 = 2x + x + 28 + (3 \times 28) \\ 400 = 3x + 112 \implies 3x = 288 \implies x = 96 \\ \text{Only English} = x = 96 \\ \text{Math Total} = M_o + B = 2x + 28 = 192 + 28 = 220 $$

questions_hin.q_hi: A fruit seller sells 40% of the oranges that he has along with 4 more oranges to a customer. he then sells 25% of the remaining oranges and 4 more oranges to second customer. he then sells 80% of the now remaining oranges to a third customer and is still left with 4 oranges. How many oranges did the fruit seller have initially?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, ulta chal! C3 ke paas jaane ke baad 4 bache, ye $20\%$ hain kyunki usko $80\%$ de diye the. Toh C3 ke paas total remaining the 20. C2 ne 4 extra liye the, wapas do = 24. Ye 24 $75\%$ the, toh total the 32. C1 ne 4 extra liye, wapas do = 36. Ye 36 $60\%$ the, toh shuru me the 60. Pure reverse thinking!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Reverse working approach.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{End: } 20\% \text{ of } R_2 = 4 \implies R_2 = 20 \\ \text{Step 2: } 75\% \text{ of } R_1 - 4 = R_2 = 20 \\ 75\% \text{ of } R_1 = 24 \implies R_1 = \frac{24}{0.75} = 32 \\ \text{Step 1: } 60\% \text{ of Initial} - 4 = R_1 = 32 \\ 60\% \text{ of Initial} = 36 \implies \text{Initial} = \frac{36}{0.6} = 60 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Forward logic basic equation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Let total } = x \\ \text{After C1: } R_1 = x - (0.4x + 4) = 0.6x - 4 \\ \text{After C2: } R_2 = R_1 - (0.25 R_1 + 4) = 0.75 R_1 - 4 \\ \text{After C3: } R_3 = R_2 - 0.8 R_2 = 0.2 R_2 \\ 0.2 R_2 = 4 \implies R_2 = 20 \\ 0.75 R_1 - 4 = 20 \implies 0.75 R_1 = 24 \implies R_1 = 32 \\ 0.6x - 4 = 32 \implies 0.6x = 36 \implies x = 60 $$

Exam Takeaway: Remaining problems me jab constant values judd rahi ho toh 'Reverse Logic' sabse accurate aur fast hoti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 40% less ka matlab uske paas 60% hai. Toh $0.6 \times 2.5 = 1.5$. Sabko ek base variable $P$ me convert kar lenge toh equation single variable ki ban jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, sabko line me laga.
$Q = 2.5P$.
$S = 60\% \text{ of } Q = 0.6 \times 2.5P = 1.5P$.
R sabka average hai: $4R = P + Q + R + S \implies 3R = P + 2.5P + 1.5P = 5P \implies R = \frac{5}{3}P$.
Ab given hai $P + R = 4800 \implies P + \frac{5}{3}P = \frac{8}{3}P = 4800 \implies P = 1800$.
Toh $R = 4800 - 1800 = 3000$. Ekdum badiya set hua!

Inka sum = 10 units. $R = \frac{10+R}{4} \implies 3R = 10 \implies R = \frac{10}{3}$.
$P+R = 2 + \frac{10}{3} = \frac{16}{3} \equiv 4800$. $1 \text{ unit} = 900$. Toh $R = \frac{10}{3} \times 900 = 3000$.

questions_hin.q_hi:
A retail store sells Premium and Casual shirts. The ratio of the price of a Premium shirt to a Casual shirt is 5:2. The ratio of the daily volume of units sold of Premium to Casual shirts is 2:15, generating a fixed combined daily revenue of $50,000.

Due to a market shift, the price of Casual shirts is increased by 20%, but their sales volume drops by 10%. To maintain the exact same total daily revenue of $50,000, by what percentage must the overall revenue generated by Premium shirts decrease?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change + Zero-Sum (JSM) Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan Revenue = Price $\times$ Volume hai. Casual shirts ke price aur volume dono me change hai, toh pehle inka single net successive nikal le. $+20$ aur $-10$ ka successive aayega $+8\%$. Ab total revenue ka ratio nikal (Premium : Casual = $10 : 30 = 1 : 3$). Casual (Base 3) ne total 8% ki vridhi ki, yani $+24$ ka deviation. Total fix rakhne ke liye Premium (Base 1) ko seedha $-24$ girna padega. Khel khatam! 50,000 bas darane ke liye hai. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle successive laga, fir JSM se balance kar de. Mathematically :-
$\text{Revenue Ratio (Prem : Cas)} = (5 \times 2) : (2 \times 15) = 10 : 30 = 1 : 3$
$\text{Casual Net Change} = 20 - 10 - \frac{20 \times 10}{100} = +8\%$
$\text{Casual Deviation} = 3 \times 8\% = +24$
$\text{Required Premium Loss} = -24$
$\% \text{ Reduction in Premium} = \frac{24}{1} = 24\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute numbers maan kar solve karna. Mathematically :-
$\text{Let Total Revenue} = 400x$
$\text{Initial Premium Rev} = 100x, \text{Casual Rev} = 300x$
$\text{New Casual Rev} = 300x \times 1.08 = 324x$
$\text{Required Premium Rev} = 400x - 324x = 76x$
$\text{Reduction in Premium} = 100x - 76x = 24x$
$\% \text{ Reduction} = \frac{24x}{100x} \times 100 = 24\%$ Exam Takeaway: Jab $A \times B$ ke dono components change hon, toh pehle Successive lagakar usko single percentage me compress kar lo. Fir Base Ratio par Zero-Sum lagao. Ye 2 steps me khatam hone wala topper method hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: The population of country A decreased by p% and the population of country B decreased by q% from the year 2020 to 2021. Here 'p' is greater than 'q'. Let 'x' be the ratio of the population of country A to the population of country B in the given year. What is the percentage decrease in 'x' from 2020 to 2021?

Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Successive Change / Variable Ratio Algebra

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Formula based hai. Ratio $x = \frac{A}{B}$. New ratio banega $x' = \frac{A(1 - \frac{p}{100})}{B(1 - \frac{q}{100})}$. Yaani old ke sath ek multiplier chipka hai $\frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Bas yahi se decrease fraction nikal lena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... New $x' = x \times \frac{100-p}{100-q}$. Decrease kitna hua? $(1 - \frac{100-p}{100-q}) \times x = \frac{(100-q) - (100-p)}{100-q} \times x = \frac{p-q}{100-q} \times x$. Percentage me badalne ke liye 100 se multiply karo base (x) ke respect me: $\frac{p-q}{100-q} \times 100$. Option A tick maar bina darr ke!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Value assume karlo. Let A=100, B=100. Let p=20, q=10. Original x=1. New A=80, New B=90. New x = $\frac{80}{90} = \frac{8}{9}$. Decrease = $1 - \frac{8}{9} = \frac{1}{9}$. Percentage decrease = $\frac{100}{9}\%$. Options me p=20, q=10 dalo. A) $\frac{100(10)}{90} = \frac{100}{9}$. Match! Baki options match nahi karenge.

Pen-Free Observation: Ye 80,000 ek bhayankar trap hai. Jab nikalna hi percentage increase hai, toh absolute numbers ko raste me laane ki zaroorat hi nahi, seedha base 100 se khelna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, absolute value ko side me rakh.
Income ko 100 maan. Expenses hue $= 40 + 20 + 20 = 80$. Save hua $= 20$.
Nayi Income ban gayi $= 120$.
Naye Expenses hue $= 44 (40 \times 1.1) + 22.4 (20 \times 1.12) + 20 = 86.4$.
Nayi Savings $= 120 - 86.4 = 33.6$.
Savings kitni badhi? $33.6 - 20 = 13.6$.
Percentage increment $= \frac{13.6}{20} \times 100 = 68\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar 80,000 ko le kar baithega toh $10880 / 16000$ jaisi bhari terms aayengi, jo answer toh $68\%$ hi dengi par tera poora time khaa jayengi.

Exam Takeaway: Percentage-to-percentage questions me real value ko hamesha ignore maarna hota hai.

Important RuleTrap to Avoid
Ignore Absolute ValuesWhen dealing purely in percentages, never calculate real values.

questions_hin.q_hi: In an adult population of a city, 40\% men and 30\% women are married. What is the percentage of married adult population if no man marries more than one woman and no woman marries more than one man; and there are no widows and widowers?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, seedha logic hai CDS aur CGL ka. 'No man marries more than one woman' ka simply matlab hai Married Men = Married Women. Toh $M:F$ ka direct inverse ratio banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weightage formula mat lagana, seedha JSM laga. Base $30\%$ pakad le aur deviation total unit me baant de. Pen-free observation se 10 second me hack ho gaya!

Mathematically :-
$$ 40\\% M = 30\\% F \\implies M:F = 3:4 \\\\ Total = 7 \\ units \\\\ Base = 30\\% \\\\ Dev = \\frac{3 \\times (40-30)}{7} = \\frac{30}{7} = 4\\frac{2}{7}\\% \\\\ Ans = 30\\% + 4\\frac{2}{7}\\% = 34\\frac{2}{7}\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan kar absolute count me equations laga aur phir percentage nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$ M = 300, F = 400 \\\\ Mar_M = 120, Mar_F = 120 \\\\ Total \\ Married = 240 \\\\ \\% = \\frac{240}{700} \\times 100 = 34\\frac{2}{7}\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Inverse ratio hamesha percentage variables ko fraction me set karta hai aur aage ka kam deviation dekhta hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: In an election, there were four candidates and 95% of voters cast their votes. One candidate got 25% of the votes while the other three shared the remaining votes in the ratio of 6:7:2. The difference of votes secured by the candidate standing 3rd to the candidate standing 4th is equal to 69198. Find the votes secured by the winning candidate.
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, vote 4 logon me batein. Ek 25\% le gaya, baaki teeno 75\% lenge. 6:7:2 ka sum hi 15 hai. 15 unit seedha 75\% se map kar, har candidate ka direct percentage aa jayega.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Remaining 75\% ko 15 units (6+7+2) me baant. 1 unit = 5\%. Teeno candidates ko mile 30\%, 35\%, aur 10\%. Ab ranks dekh: 1st=35\%, 2nd=30\%, 3rd=25\% (jo pehle alag kiya tha), 4th=10\%. 3rd aur 4th ka margin: $25\% - 10\% = 15\%$. Ye 15\% = 69198 diya hai. Winner ko pucha hai (yani 35\%). Toh $\frac{69198}{15} \times 35 = 69198 \times \frac{7}{3}$. Unit digit laga! $\frac{69198}{3} = 23066$, last me 6 hai, aur $6 \times 7 = 42$ aakhiri me 2 aayega. Options me sirf 161462 me end me 2 hai. Khatam!

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Jab tu percentages ko ratios ke total se equating karta hai, toh calculation 2x fast ho jati hai. Uske baad Unit Digit aur Divisibility hi lagana hota hai final multiply karne ki jagah.

**Exam Takeaway:** Ratios ko actual percentages ke equal rakhkar common multiplier nikalna seekh aur end me unit digit se khel kar pura multiply bachaya kar.

Candidate RankVote Percentage
A. 1st (Winner)1. $35\%$
B. Difference (3rd & 4th)2. $25\% - 10\% = 15\%$
